title: Symmetry and Parity of a Rational Function
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Symmetry and Parity
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Test the function g(x) = \frac{x}{x^2 - 1} algebraically for even and odd symmetry, and describe the geometric symmetry of its graph.
finalAnswer: Odd function; symmetric with respect to the origin

steps.title: Substitute -x into the Formula
steps.explanation: Replace every occurrence of x in the rational formula with -x to evaluate the reflected output.
steps.why: Testing for function parity begins by computing the response of the rule to the negated input -x.

steps.title: Simplify the Exponents
steps.explanation: Because squaring a negative number yields a positive result, (-x)^2 = x^2, leaving the denominator unchanged while the numerator is negated.
steps.why: Even powers of real numbers are invariant under negation: (-x)^2 = x^2.

steps.title: Compare with -g(x)
steps.explanation: Moving the negative sign in the numerator to the front of the entire fraction establishes that g(-x) = -g(x) for all x in the domain (x != 1 and x != -1).
steps.why: The quotient of an odd function (numerator x) and an even function (denominator x^2 - 1) is an odd function.

steps.title: Conclude Symmetry
steps.mathExpression: g(-x) = -g(x) \implies \text{Symmetry with respect to the origin}
steps.explanation: Since g(-x) = -g(x), the function is odd. The graph is invariant under a 180-degree rotation about the origin.
steps.why: Origin symmetry is the characteristic geometric manifestation of every odd function.
